body.text: FATAL ASSAULT IN POONCH DISTRICT SPARKS OUTCRY

The United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) has issued a stern statement strongly condemning a fatal armed attack on a vehicle carrying political activists in Poonch district. The assault, which took place on the night of June 5, resulted in the death of one individual and left a prominent civic leader injured.

According to verified local dispatches, the vehicle was targeted near Barmanag while returning from Khaigala to Rawalakot. Among the occupants was Umar Nazir, a Core Committee Member of the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), who sustained injuries during the shooting. His close associate, media adviser, and trusted companion, Shahzaib Habib, succumbed to fatal injuries.

Declaring the Awami Action Committee a terrorist organization is the worst form of oppression. UKPNP unequivocally opposes violence, whether perpetrated by a state, an institution, a group, or an individual.

In an official address, UKPNP Chairman Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri extended his heartfelt condolences to the family of Shahzaib Habib and expressed hopes for the rapid recovery of Umar Nazir. The party chairman called upon relevant law enforcement and judicial authorities to conduct a transparent, impartial, and immediate investigation to prosecute those responsible.

items: Immediate, independent probe into the Barmanag armed ambush near Rawalakot
Full accountability and prosecution of perpetrators without administrative delay
Appeals for public calm and restraint, upholding peaceful democratic engagement
Adherence to nonviolent political struggle despite severe provocation

body.text: Kashmiri highlighted that despite the loss of his close companion, Umar Nazir publicly appealed to supporters for calm and nonviolence. The UKPNP chairman praised this response as a testament to mature, peaceful political struggle, reiterating that the JAAC must continue championing fundamental civil rights exclusively through democratic avenues.
PUSHBACK AGAINST PROSCRIPTION OF THE AWAMI ACTION COMMITTEE

The UKPNP expressed grave concern over recent administrative steps declaring the Joint Awami Action Committee a proscribed entity. Chairman Kashmiri characterized the decree as a draconian and undemocratic measure that directly infringes upon basic international human rights standards.

The leadership noted that the decision marks an abrupt policy shift, coming shortly after high-level negotiations took place between representatives of the Government of Pakistan, the Azad Jammu and Kashmir administration, and JAAC delegates.

items: Direct official dialogue between state authorities and JAAC delegates continued until May 30, 2026
Government ministers publicly addressed JAAC members in constructive, non-adversarial terms
No major security infractions or violent incidents were recorded during the dialogue period
Sudden reclassification of the civic body as a proscribed organization raises urgent legal concerns

body.text: Freedoms of peaceful assembly, association, and expression are fundamental rights protected under global covenants, including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the ICCPR.

Addressing the broader political climate across Azad Jammu and Kashmir, the UKPNP urged authorities to lift arbitrary restrictions on democratic expression. The party stressed that state intimidation and civic suppression serve only to worsen public grievances and heighten regional instability.

Simultaneously, the UKPNP advised JAAC leadership to periodically review its operational strategies—including nuanced discussions surrounding the 12 reserved seats for Kashmiri refugees—to ensure public demands remain aligned with inclusive, peaceful, and constitutional principles.

items: Strict instruction to party cadres to avoid spreading unverified reports or altered media
Ban on disseminating AI-generated content or speculative rumors surrounding the attack
Directive to rely exclusively on official UKPNP channels for fact-based developments
Continuous monitoring of regional legal procedures by international human rights observers

body.text: The statement concluded with a firm directive to all party members and civil society activists to maintain strict vigilance against disinformation, reaffirming that principled, fact-based journalism remains essential to safeguarding justice and fundamental human dignity.
